newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU's Kinnock slams Russian air transit fees.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock slams Russian air transit fees.

text.p: European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock hit out on Tuesday against the fees faced by European airlines overflying Siberia en route to north east Asia, branding them illegal and unjustified.

"Clearly it's completely unjustified, clearly it's not within international law or common practice and clearly it cannot go on without much greater resistance," Kinnock told a news conference after a meeting of EU transport ministers.

He urged a three-pronged campaign to lower the fees, which the Association of European Airlines said in its 1997 report amounted to $225 million a year or an additional six percent on operating costs for the route.

The Commissioner said several ministers spoke out on the issue during Tuesday's meeting and suggested airlines continue their campaign against the charges while the European Commission and member states made their own representations to the Russians in all bilateral contacts.
Kinnock said European Commission President Jacques Santer would raise the issue with Russian President Viktor Chernomyrdin during the latter's scheduled visit to Brussels on July 18.
